descriptions.Araneae: a spider or other arachnid with eight legs and two main body segments, without wings
descriptions.Coleoptera: a beetle with a compact body and hard protective wing covers, also called elytra
descriptions.Diptera: a true fly with one visible pair of functional wings and a compact insect body
descriptions.Hemiptera: a true bug with a piercing-sucking mouthpart and a small to medium insect body
descriptions.Hymenoptera: a bee, wasp, or ant with a segmented body and typically two pairs of membranous wings
descriptions.Lepidoptera: a butterfly or moth with broad wings covered in fine scales
descriptions.Odonata: a dragonfly or damselfly with a long abdomen, large eyes, and transparent wings
descriptions.aeroplane: a fixed-wing aircraft with a fuselage, wings, and tail, viewed from any angle
descriptions.bicycle: a human-powered two-wheeled vehicle with a frame, pedals, handlebar, and wheels
descriptions.bird: a feathered animal with a beak, wings, and a visible body or head
descriptions.boat: a watercraft with a hull, usually floating on water
descriptions.bottle: a portable container with a narrow neck and an opening at the top
descriptions.bus: a large road vehicle for carrying passengers, usually with a long body and multiple windows
descriptions.car: a four-wheeled passenger automobile with a roof, body, and windows
descriptions.cat: a small domesticated feline with pointed ears, a face, and a tail
descriptions.chair: a single-seat piece of furniture with a seat and a backrest, often supported by legs
descriptions.cow: a large domesticated bovine with four legs, a broad body, and a head with a muzzle
descriptions.diningtable: a table with a broad flat top and supporting legs, intended for eating or dining
descriptions.dog: a domesticated canine with a muzzle, four legs, and a tail
descriptions.horse: a large four-legged equine with a long neck, mane, and tail
descriptions.motorbike: a motorized two-wheeled vehicle with a frame, seat, handlebar, and wheels
descriptions.person: a human being, including a visible head, torso, arms, legs, or full body
descriptions.pottedplant: a living plant growing from a visible pot or other plant container
descriptions.sheep: a woolly domesticated ruminant with four legs, a rounded body, and a short head
descriptions.sofa: an upholstered multi-seat couch with a long seat, backrest, and armrests
descriptions.train: a rail vehicle or a connected series of rail cars traveling on railway tracks
descriptions.tvmonitor: an electronic display screen with a rectangular panel and surrounding bezel
descriptions.fish: an aquatic animal with a streamlined body, fins, scales, and a visible head or tail
descriptions.crazing: a network of fine, shallow, branching cracks forming a web-like pattern on a steel surface
descriptions.inclusion: an irregular non-metallic particle or embedded foreign region inside the steel surface
descriptions.patches: an irregular localized patch of different texture, brightness, or oxidation on the steel surface
descriptions.pitted_surface: a steel surface containing multiple small cavities, pits, or shallow circular depressions
descriptions.rolled-in_scale: an elongated scale-like oxide or rough defect pressed into the steel during rolling
descriptions.scratches: thin elongated grooves or score marks running across the steel surface
descriptions.scallop: a fan-shaped bivalve shell with radiating ridges, seen on the underwater seafloor
descriptions.seacucumber: an elongated, soft-bodied marine animal with a cylindrical cucumber-like shape
descriptions.seaurchin: a rounded marine animal covered with many prominent spines
descriptions.Expressway-Service-area: a roadside service area beside an expressway, with buildings, parking, or access roads
descriptions.Expressway-toll-station: a toll plaza across an expressway, with toll booths or lanes under a canopy
descriptions.airplane: a fixed-wing aircraft with a fuselage, wings, and tail, viewed in an aerial image
descriptions.airport: an airport complex containing runways, taxiways, terminals, or aircraft parking areas
descriptions.baseballfield: a baseball diamond with a dirt infield, grass outfield, and surrounding foul territory
descriptions.basketballcourt: a rectangular sports court with painted boundary lines and basketball markings
descriptions.bridge: a structure carrying a road or railway across water, a valley, or another transport route
descriptions.chimney: a tall narrow chimney or industrial stack rising from a building or facility
descriptions.dam: a large barrier built across a river or waterway, often next to a reservoir
descriptions.golffield: a golf course area with fairways, greens, sand hazards, or distinctive mowed patterns
descriptions.groundtrackfield: an athletic track-and-field complex with an oval running track and an infield
descriptions.harbor: a sheltered waterfront or port with docks, piers, moored vessels, or enclosed water
descriptions.overpass: an elevated road or railway crossing above another road, railway, or ground-level route
descriptions.ship: a large vessel with a hull, superstructure, or deck, usually visible on water
descriptions.stadium: a large sports arena with a central field and surrounding stands or seating
descriptions.storagetank: a large industrial storage tank, often cylindrical with a circular roof or top
descriptions.tenniscourt: a rectangular tennis court with a central net and clearly marked playing lines
descriptions.trainstation: a railway station with platforms, tracks, station buildings, or a train terminal
descriptions.vehicle: a road vehicle such as a car, truck, or bus, viewed from above
descriptions.windmill: a tall tower or structure topped with several long radial blades
